body.statement: Determine the parameterized complexity of numerical edge identification on feasible rational acyclic mixed-graph instances with \(K_G\le k\): does the handle \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) yield an algorithm with bit complexity \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\), or is the promise problem \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard for some fixed \(k\)? Any resolution must preserve exact fibers through singular component domains rather than assume genericity.
body.justification: This question exposes the genuine open content between a global maximum-indegree dichotomy and practically near-forest graphs.
body.gap: The published unrestricted reduction and generic tree algorithms do not parameterize the number of two-parent vertices, and the selected compiler uses a number of such vertices that grows with the arithmetic circuit.
body.consumer: MIIV and latent-to-observed workflows with a small number of multi-parent equations would obtain either a fixed-parameter exact audit or a certified obstruction showing that even this regime is intractable.
